title: INT8 weight-only tensor-delta audit and calibration pipeline for GPTQ/AWQ
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Build an automated validation and calibration pipeline that integrates GPTQ/AWQ weight-only profiles into CI, producing per-layer tensor-delta audit traces and quantitative accuracy regressions versus floating-point baselines. The pipeline should surface real degradations (statistically significant), enable rapid rollback, and provide deterministic artifacts for postmortems.
background: We have multiple upstream efforts creating weight-only INT8 profiles for open models (GPTQ/AWQ variants). Past regressions were often subtle: small per-layer quantization errors that accumulate under long-context generation or rare prompt shapes. Existing regtests focus on end-to-end metrics but lack a white-box per-tensor audit and an automated calibration step that can tune clip/scale heuristics across shards. This ticket defines an orchestration and test harness to close that gap and make CI-level gating practical.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline runs in CI on push to quant-profiles and produces a compact artifact: per-layer tensor-delta CSV, summary report, and flagged regressions
Regression flagging uses a configurable statistical threshold (default: p<0.01) on primary metrics (perplexity for LM, EM/F1 on eval sets, embedding cosine) compared to fp32 baseline
Automated calibration step (sharder-level) can apply stored calibration matrices or run a fast 1-2 epoch micro-calibration on a golden prompt shard without exceeding 10% CI runtime budget
Artifacts are stored to S3 with immutable paths and linked in the Linear ticket and PRs; diagnostics include top-5 layers contributing to tensor-delta and sample prompts that trigger drift
Rollback policy documented: auto-mark build failed + recommend fallback variant (quantized with per-channel corrections or FP fallback) when high-severity regressions appear
Owners can run a local reproducible smoke command that executes the pipeline on a single GPU with a 15-minute timeout
tasks: Design tensor-delta format and minimal schema (layer name, param-shape, mean abs delta, max abs delta, scaled score)
Implement lightweight per-layer delta collector in the runtime (opt-in flag --collect-tensor-deltas)
Add CI job that runs: build quant profile, run inference on golden prompt set, compute metrics vs fp32 baseline, upload artifacts
Create a micro-calibration runner that accepts either stored calibration matrices or runs on a small shard of calibration prompts
Integrate thresholding rules and produce human-readable summary with top contributors and recommended actions
Add alerting hooks to PRs (comment with S3 links) and annotate Linear ticket automatically on failure
Document fail/rollback playbook and include sample command lines for on-call to validate and revert a profile
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for tensor-delta collector (synthetic tensors with known deltas). 2) CI smoke: run pipeline on a small open-source model (e.g., Llama-7B toy) comparing INT8-GPTQ and INT8-AWQ against fp32; verify artifact generation. 3) Statistical regression harness: run N=5 seeds on the golden prompt set to compute confidence intervals for perplexity and embedding cosine. 4) End-to-end durability: run long-context generation test (context length=8k) to detect accumulation regressions. 5) Nightly full-run against curated eval (SQuAD, MMLU subset, summarization prompts) to track drift over time.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge feature branch behind runtime flag and enable on quant-profiles CI only. Phase 2: Enable on nightly pipeline; collect two weeks of baseline metrics. Phase 3: Enable gating with a soft-fail for one cycle (notify authors) then hard-fail if no exceptions. Phase 4: Integrate into canary deploys for Dedicated region with auto-fallback to FP fallback variant if high-severity regression observed.
monitoring_slo: Quant-profile CI must complete within 90 minutes for full-run, 12 minutes for smoke-run; artifact upload success >= 99%. Regression false positive rate target < 5% (measured against manual triage over 30 days).
risks: Calibration runtime could exceed CI budgets if not shard-limited; mitigated by micro-calibration and cached matrices
Statistical noise could cause noisy failures on small eval sets; mitigate via multiple seeds and effect-size thresholds
Additional instrumentation may slightly change runtime characteristics in canary; runtime-flag ensures production unaffected
Large artifact storage may increase S3 costs; keep per-run artifact footprint < 5MB by using aggregated CSVs and compressed summaries
notes: Tensor-delta scoring uses layer-norm scaled mean-abs-diff to normalize across parameter scales
We will include a small set of adversarial prompts designed to expose per-layer sensitivity (constructed from historical regressions)
For AWQ, include a matrix that records per-shard scaling factors so calibration can apply shard-level offsets
Discussed with Research: agreed to prioritize reproducibility over micro-optimizations in the first iteration
